sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āpto vivādaḥ paramo viśāṃ pate; na vidyate kiṃ cana matsya hīnataḥ na me jitaḥ kaś cana dhārayed dhanaṃ; varo mamaiṣo 'stu tava prasādataḥ
english: Yudhishthira said: The highest outcome of a contest has been obtained, O lord of the people; nothing whatsoever is lacking, O Matsya. No one whom I have defeated retains the winnings — let this be my boon, by your grace.

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca hanyām avadhyaṃ yadi te 'priyaṃ caret; pravrājayeyaṃ viṣayād dvijāṃs tathā śṛṇvantu me jānapadāḥ samāgatāḥ; kaṅko yathāhaṃ viṣaye prabhus tathā
english: Virata said: I would strike down even one who should not be struck, should he act against your wish; likewise I would banish Brahmins from the realm. Let the assembled people of the land hear this: as I am master of the kingdom, so too is Kanka.

sanskrit: samānayāno bhavitāsi me sakhā; prabhūtavastro bahupānabhojanaḥ paśyes tvam antaś ca bahiś ca sarvadā; kṛtaṃ ca te dvāram apāvṛtaṃ mayā
english: You shall be my companion and friend of equal standing; you shall have abundant garments, drink, and food. You may move freely both within and without at all times, and I have made the door open for you.

sanskrit: ye tvānuvādeyur avṛttikarśitā; brūyāś ca teṣāṃ vacanena me sadā dāsyāmi sarvaṃ tad ahaṃ na saṃśayo; na te bhayaṃ vidyati saṃnidhau mama
english: Those who might speak ill of you, though worn down by want — you need only mention them to me and I will provide them everything, there is no doubt. No fear exists for you in my presence.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ sa labdhvā tu varaṃ samāgamaṃ; virāṭarājena nararṣabhas tadā uvāsa vīraḥ paramārcitaḥ sukhī; na cāpi kaś cic caritaṃ bubodha tat
english: Vaishampayana said: Having thus obtained the boon and the fellowship of King Virata, that bull among men, that hero, lived there highly honored and happy; and no one at all came to know his true conduct.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athāparo bhīmabalaḥ śriyā jvalann; upāyayau siṃhavilāsavikramaḥ khajaṃ ca darvīṃ ca kareṇa dhārayann; asiṃ ca kālāṅgam akośam avraṇam
english: Vaishampayana said: Then another came, blazing with the splendor of mighty strength, striding with the gait and grace of a lion — he held in his hand a ladle, a stirring rod, and a dark-bladed sword unsheathed and unblemished.

sanskrit: sa sūdarūpaḥ parameṇa varcasā; ravir yathā lokam imaṃ prabhāsayan sukṛṣṇavāsā girirājasāravān; sa matsyarājaṃ samupetya tasthivān
english: In the guise of a cook, yet blazing with supreme radiance like the sun illumining this world, clad in dark garments and firm as the king of mountains, he came and stood before the king of the Matsyas.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya rājā varayann upāgataṃ; tato 'bravīj jānapadān samāgatān siṃhonnatāṃso 'yam atīva rūpavān; pradṛśyate ko nu nararṣabho yuvā
english: The king, beholding him as he approached and wishing to honor him, then spoke to the assembled people of the land: "This one with shoulders raised like a lion's is exceedingly handsome — who is this bull among men, this youth?"

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaḥ puruṣo ravir yathā; vitarkayan nāsya labhāmi saṃpadam tathāsya cittaṃ hy api saṃvitarkayan; nararṣabhasyādya na yāmi tattvataḥ
english: "This is a man I have never seen before, like the sun. Pondering, I cannot fathom his fortune; and pondering likewise his disposition, I cannot to this day arrive at the truth about this bull among men."

sanskrit: tato virāṭaṃ samupetya pāṇḍavaḥ; sudīnarūpo vacanaṃ mahāmanāḥ uvāca sūdo 'smi narendra ballavo; bhajasva māṃ vyañjanakāram uttamam
english: Then the Pandava, approaching Virata with a seemingly humble appearance yet great in spirit, said: "I am a cook, O king of men, Ballava by name — accept me as a master preparer of dishes."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca na sūdatāṃ mānada śraddadhāmi te; sahasranetrapratimo hi dṛśyase śriyā ca rūpeṇa ca vikrameṇa ca; prabhāsi tātānavaro nareṣv iha
english: Virata said: "I do not believe in your being a cook, O giver of honor; for you appear like Indra of a thousand eyes in splendor, in form, and in valor. You shine here as second to none among men, my friend."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca narendra sūdaḥ paricārako 'smi te; jānāmi sūpān prathamena kevalān āsvāditā ye nṛpate purābhavan; yudhiṣṭhireṇāpi nṛpeṇa sarvaśaḥ
english: Bhima said: "O king of men, I am your cook and servant. I know the art of soups and dishes perfectly — those same dishes that were once tasted with pleasure, O king, by King Yudhishthira in every respect."

sanskrit: balena tulyaś ca na vidyate mayā; niyuddhaśīlaś ca sadaiva pārthiva gajaiś ca siṃhaiś ca sameyivān ahaṃ; sadā kariṣyāmi tavānagha priyam
english: "None is found equal to me in strength; I am ever fond of wrestling, O king, and I have contended with elephants and lions alike. I shall always do what is pleasing to you, O blameless one."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca dadāmi te hanta varaṃ mahānase; tathā ca kuryāḥ kuśalaṃ hi bhāṣase na caiva manye tava karma tat samaṃ; samudranemiṃ pṛthivīṃ tvam arhasi
english: Virata said: "Very well, I grant you the boon of the kitchen; work there as you wish, for you speak skillfully. Yet I do not think that work suits you at all — you deserve the earth girdled by the sea."

sanskrit: yathā hi kāmas tava tat tathā kṛtaṃ; mahānase tvaṃ bhava me puraskṛtaḥ narāś ca ye tatra mamocitāḥ purā; bhavasva teṣām adhipo mayā kṛtaḥ
english: "As your desire is, so it shall be done — be foremost for me in the kitchen. And the men who were formerly my appointed ones there — be you, by my decree, their master."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā sa bhīmo vihito mahānase; virāṭarājño dayito 'bhavad dṛḍham uvāsa rājan na ca taṃ pṛthagjano; bubodha tatrānucaraś ca kaś cana
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus Bhima, installed in the kitchen, became the firm favorite of King Virata. He dwelt there, O king, and no ordinary person, nor any attendant there, came to know him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ keśān samutkṣipya vellitāgrān aninditān jugūha dakṣiṇe pārśve mṛdūn asitalocanā
english: Vaishampayana said: Then she, the dark-eyed one, gathering up her tresses whose tips were curled and which were beyond reproach, concealed them along her right side, those soft locks.

sanskrit: vāsaś ca paridhāyaikaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sumalinaṃ mahat kṛtvā veṣaṃ ca sairandhryāḥ kṛṣṇā vyacarad ārtavat
english: And donning a single great dark and very soiled garment, and taking on the disguise of a sairandhri (a skilled female attendant), Krishnaa moved about as one in distress.

sanskrit: tāṃ narāḥ paridhāvantīṃ striyaś ca samupādravan apṛcchaṃś caiva tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kā tvaṃ kiṃ ca cikīrṣasi
english: Men and women ran toward her as she moved about; and seeing her, they questioned her: "Who are you, and what do you wish to do?"

sanskrit: sā tān uvāca rājendra sairandhry aham upāgatā karma cecchāmi vai kartuṃ tasya yo māṃ pupukṣati
english: She said to them: "O lord of kings, I have come as a sairandhri; I wish to do service for whoever will take me in."

sanskrit: tasyā rūpeṇa veṣeṇa ślakṣṇayā ca tathā girā nāśraddadhata tāṃ dāsīm annahetor upasthitām
english: Because of her beauty, her bearing, and her sweet speech, they did not believe that she was a maidservant come merely for food.

sanskrit: virāṭasya tu kaikeyī bhāryā paramasaṃmatā avalokayantī dadṛśe prāsādād drupadātmajām
english: But Kaikeyi, the greatly honored wife of Virata, looking out from the palace, caught sight of the daughter of Drupada.

sanskrit: sā samīkṣya tathārūpām anāthām ekavāsasam samāhūyābravīd bhadre kā tvaṃ kiṃ ca cikīrṣasi
english: She, having observed her of such beauty, unprotected and clad in but a single garment, called to her and said: "Blessed one, who are you and what do you wish to do?"

sanskrit: sā tām uvāca rājendra sairandhry aham upāgatā karma cecchāmy ahaṃ kartuṃ tasya yo māṃ pupukṣati
english: She said to her: "O queen, I have come as a sairandhri; I wish to serve whoever will take me in."

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca naivaṃrūpā bhavanty evaṃ yathā vadasi bhāmini preṣayanti ca vai dāsīr dāsāṃś caivaṃvidhān bahūn
english: Sudeshna said: "Those who are as you describe yourself — maidservants — are not of such beauty, O lovely one; many send out maidservants and manservants of that kind."

sanskrit: gūḍhagulphā saṃhatorus trigambhīrā ṣaḍunnatā raktā pañcasu rakteṣu haṃsagadgadabhāṣiṇī
english: "Your ankles are hidden, your thighs compact, three things about you are deep, six are elevated, five are red in their redness, and you speak with the sweet broken voice of a swan."

sanskrit: sukeśī sustanī śyāmā pīnaśroṇipayodharā tena tenaiva saṃpannā kāśmīrīva turaṃgamā
english: "You have beautiful hair, well-formed breasts, a dark complexion, full hips and bosom, and you are endowed with every quality — like a Kashmiri mare in her excellence."

sanskrit: svarālapakṣmanayanā bimboṣṭhī tanumadhyamā kambugrīvā gūḍhasirā pūrṇacandranibhānanā
english: "Your eyes are bright with lovely lashes, your lips like the bimba fruit, your waist slender, your neck like a conch shell, your veins hidden, and your face like the full moon."

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ brūhi yathā bhadre nāsi dāsī kathaṃ cana yakṣī vā yadi vā devī gandharvī yadi vāpsarāḥ
english: "Tell me truly, blessed one — you are by no means a maidservant. Are you a yakshi, or a goddess, a gandharvi, or an apsara?"

sanskrit: alambusā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkātha mālinī indrāṇī vāruṇī vā tvaṃ tvaṣṭur dhātuḥ prajāpateḥ devyo deveṣu vikhyātās tāsāṃ tvaṃ katamā śubhe
english: "Are you Alambusa, Mishrakesha, Pundarika, or Malini? Are you Indrani, Varuni, or a goddess of Tvashtr, Dhata, or Prajapati? Those goddesses are renowned among the gods — which of them are you, auspicious one?"

sanskrit: draupady uvāca nāsmi devī na gandharvī nāsurī na ca rākṣasī sairandhrī tu bhujiṣyāsmi satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Draupadi said: "I am not a goddess, nor a gandharvi, nor an asuri, nor a rakshasi — I am indeed a sairandhri, a free attendant. This is the truth I tell you."

sanskrit: keśāñ jānāmy ahaṃ kartuṃ piṃṣe sādhu vilepanam grathayiṣye vicitrāś ca srajaḥ paramaśobhanāḥ
english: "I know how to dress hair; I grind fragrant unguents well; and I shall weave garlands of varied flowers of the most beautiful kind."

sanskrit: ārādhayaṃ satyabhāmāṃ kṛṣṇasya mahiṣīṃ priyām kṛṣṇāṃ ca bhāryāṃ pāṇḍūnāṃ kurūṇām ekasundarīm
english: "I served Satyabhama, the beloved chief queen of Krishna, and also Krishnaa, the wife of the Pandavas, the one beauty among the Kurus."

sanskrit: tatra tatra carāmy evaṃ labhamānā suśobhanam vāsāṃsi yāvac ca labhe tāvat tāvad rame tathā
english: "I move thus from place to place, receiving beautiful garments wherever I can obtain them, and wherever I receive them, there I dwell in happiness."

sanskrit: mālinīty eva me nāma svayaṃ devī cakāra sā sāham abhyāgatā devi sudeṣṇe tvanniveśanam
english: "Malini is the very name the goddess herself gave me. It is thus that I, O goddess Sudeshna, have come to your dwelling."

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca mūrdhni tvāṃ vāsayeyaṃ vai saṃśayo me na vidyate no ced iha tu rājā tvāṃ gacchet sarveṇa cetasā
english: Sudeshna said: "I would shelter you on my very head — there is no doubt of that — were it not that the king here might pursue you with his entire heart."

sanskrit: striyo rājakule paśya yāś cemā mama veśmani prasaktās tvāṃ nirīkṣante pumāṃsaṃ kaṃ na mohayeḥ
english: "Look at the women of the royal household here in my chambers — they gaze fixedly at you. What man would you not bewitch?"

sanskrit: vṛkṣāṃś cāvasthitān paśya ya ime mama veśmani te 'pi tvāṃ saṃnamantīva pumāṃsaṃ kaṃ na mohayeḥ
english: "Look at the trees standing here in my dwelling — even they seem to bow toward you. What man would you not enchant?"

sanskrit: rājā virāṭaḥ suśroṇi dṛṣṭvā vapur amānuṣam vihāya māṃ varārohe tvāṃ gacchet sarvacetasā
english: "King Virata, seeing your superhuman form, O fair-hipped one, would abandon me, O woman of lovely limbs, and pursue you with his whole mind."

sanskrit: yaṃ hi tvam anavadyāṅgi naram āyatalocane prasaktam abhivīkṣethāḥ sa kāmavaśago bhavet
english: "Whatever man you, O flawless-limbed one with long eyes, were to gaze upon with longing — he would fall under the power of desire."

sanskrit: yaś ca tvāṃ satataṃ paśyet puruṣaś cāruhāsini evaṃ sarvānavadyāṅgi sa cānaṅgavaśo bhavet
english: "And whatever man were constantly to behold you, O one of lovely smile, of such entirely flawless limbs — he too would fall under the sway of the god of love."

sanskrit: yathā karkaṭakī garbham ādhatte mṛtyum ātmanaḥ tathāvidham ahaṃ manye vāsaṃ tava śucismite
english: "As a female crab bears in her womb her own death, so I regard your dwelling here to be of that nature, O bright-smiled one."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca nāsmi labhyā virāṭena na cānyena kathaṃ cana gandharvāḥ patayo mahyaṃ yuvānaḥ pañca bhāmini
english: Draupadi said: "I cannot be obtained by Virata, nor by any other, in any manner. My husbands are five Gandharvas who are young, O lovely one."

sanskrit: putrā gandharvarājasya mahāsattvasya kasya cit rakṣanti te ca māṃ nityaṃ duḥkhācārā tathā nv aham
english: "They are sons of a certain great-souled king of the Gandharvas; they protect me always — and so those who behave harshly toward me suffer for it, and so indeed do I."

sanskrit: yo me na dadyād ucchiṣṭaṃ na ca pādau pradhāvayet prīyeyus tena vāsena gandharvāḥ patayo mama
english: "The one who would not give me his leavings, nor bow to wash my feet — my Gandharva husbands are pleased with such a dwelling for me."

sanskrit: yo hi māṃ puruṣo gṛdhyed yathānyāḥ prākṛtastriyaḥ tām eva sa tato rātriṃ praviśed aparāṃ tanum
english: "Whatever man might lust after me as he would after any ordinary woman — that very night he would enter another body (i.e., meet his death)."

sanskrit: na cāpy ahaṃ cālayituṃ śakyā kena cid aṅgane duḥkhaśīlā hi gandharvās te ca me balavattarāḥ
english: "Nor can I be led astray by anyone, O beautiful one, for those Gandharvas are fierce in nature and are far more powerful than I."

sanskrit: sudeṣṇovāca evaṃ tvāṃ vāsayiṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ nandinīcchasi na ca pādau na cocchiṣṭaṃ sprakṣyasi tvaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: Sudeshna said: "I shall shelter you on such terms as you yourself desire, O Nandini; you shall never be made to touch feet, nor shall you ever in any way touch leavings."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ kṛṣṇā virāṭasya bhāryayā parisāntvitā na caināṃ veda tatrānyas tattvena janamejaya
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus Krishnaa was kindly reassured by the wife of Virata; and no one else there, O Janamejaya, came to know her true identity.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sahadevo 'pi gopānāṃ kṛtvā veṣam anuttamam bhāṣāṃ caiṣāṃ samāsthāya virāṭam upayād atha
english: Vaishampayana said: Sahadeva too, donning the best disguise of a cowherd and adopting their manner of speech, then approached Virata.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya bhrājamānaṃ nararṣabham samupasthāya vai rājā papraccha kurunandanam
english: Beholding him approaching and radiant, that bull among men, the king drew near and questioned the delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: kasya vā tvaṃ kuto vā tvaṃ kiṃ vā tāta cikīrṣasi na hi me dṛṣṭapūrvas tvaṃ tattvaṃ brūhi nararṣabha
english: "Whose are you, and from where do you come, and what do you wish to do, my friend? I have not seen you before — tell me truly, O bull among men."

sanskrit: sa prāpya rājānam amitratāpanas; tato 'bravīn meghamahaughaniḥsvanaḥ vaiśyo 'smi nāmnāham ariṣṭanemir; gosaṃkhya āsaṃ kurupuṃgavānām
english: He, the scorcher of enemies, having reached the king, then spoke with a voice resonant as the great roar of thunderclouds: "I am a Vaishya; Arishtanemi is my name; I was the cattle-counter of the foremost Kurus."

sanskrit: vastuṃ tvayīcchāmi viśāṃ variṣṭha; tān rājasiṃhān na hi vedmi pārthān na śakyate jīvitum anyakarmaṇā; na ca tvad anyo mama rocate nṛpaḥ
english: "I wish to dwell with you, O best among the Vaishas; for I do not know where those lions among kings, the Parthas, are. It is not possible to live by any other work, and no other king pleases me besides you."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca tvaṃ brāhmaṇo yadi vā kṣatriyo 'si; samudranemīśvararūpavān asi ācakṣva me tattvam amitrakarśana; na vaiśyakarma tvayi vidyate samam
english: Virata said: "Whether you are a Brahmin or a Kshatriya, you are endowed with the form of a lord who rules the earth girdled by the sea. Tell me truly, O crusher of enemies — the work of a Vaishya does not suit you at all."

sanskrit: kasyāsi rājño viṣayād ihāgataḥ; kiṃ cāpi śilpaṃ tava vidyate kṛtam kathaṃ tvam asmāsu nivatsyase sadā; vadasva kiṃ cāpi taveha vetanam
english: "From whose king's realm have you come here? And what skill have you cultivated? How will you dwell among us always? Tell me also what your wages should be here."

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca pañcānāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ jyeṣṭho rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tasyāṣṭaśatasāhasrā gavāṃ vargāḥ śataṃ śatāḥ
english: Sahadeva said: "The eldest of the five sons of Pandu is King Yudhishthira. His cattle herds numbered eight hundred thousand, in groups of hundreds upon hundreds."

sanskrit: apare daśasāhasrā dvis tāvantas tathāpare teṣāṃ gosaṃkhya āsaṃ vai tantipāleti māṃ viduḥ
english: "Others numbered ten thousand, and yet others twice as many. I was the cattle-counter of those herds — Tantipala is the name by which I am known."

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca yac ca saṃkhyāgataṃ kva cit na me 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cit samantād daśayojanam
english: "What has been, what is, and what will be, and whatever tally exists anywhere — there is nothing unknown to me within ten leagues in every direction."

sanskrit: guṇāḥ suviditā hy āsan mama tasya mahātmanaḥ āsīc ca sa mayā tuṣṭaḥ kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "My qualities were well known to that great-souled one, and King Yudhishthira, the Kuru king, was pleased with me."

sanskrit: kṣipraṃ hi gāvo bahulā bhavanti; na tāsu rogo bhavatīha kaś cit tais tair upāyair viditaṃ mayaitad; etāni śilpāni mayi sthitāni
english: "By this means and that, all known to me, cattle swiftly multiply; no disease whatsoever afflicts them here. These skills reside in me."

sanskrit: vṛṣabhāṃś cāpi jānāmi rājan pūjitalakṣaṇān yeṣāṃ mūtram upāghrāya api vandhyā prasūyate
english: "I know also the bulls of auspicious marks, O king — those whose urine, when smelled, can cause even a barren cow to give birth."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca śataṃ sahasrāṇi samāhitāni; varṇasya varṇasya viniścitā guṇaiḥ paśūn sapālān bhavate dadāmy ahaṃ; tvadāśrayā me paśavo bhavantv iha
english: Virata said: "A hundred thousand head of cattle gathered together — of each class and variety, their qualities ascertained — I give to you along with their herdsmen. Let my cattle here be under your care."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā sa rājño 'vidito viśāṃ pate; uvāsa tatraiva sukhaṃ nareśvaraḥ na cainam anye 'pi viduḥ kathaṃ cana; prādāc ca tasmai bharaṇaṃ yathepsitam
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus that lord of men, unknown to the king, O lord of the people, dwelt there in comfort. And no others either came to know him in any way; and the king gave him maintenance as he desired.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athāparo 'dṛśyata rūpasaṃpadā; strīṇām alaṃkāradharo bṛhat pumān prākāravapre pratimucya kuṇḍale; dīrghe ca kambū parihāṭake śubhe
english: Vaishampayana said: Then another appeared — a great man in the full splendor of his form, wearing women's ornaments, with earrings fastened at his ears on the rampart-top, and wearing long beautiful conch-shell bangles and bracelets.

sanskrit: bahūṃś ca dīrghāṃś ca vikīrya mūrdhajān; mahābhujo vāraṇamattavikramaḥ gatena bhūmim abhikampayaṃs tadā; virāṭam āsādya sabhāsamīpataḥ
english: He shook out many long tresses upon his head; great-armed, he moved with the gait of a rut elephant, making the earth tremble with his step; and he came up to Virata near the hall of assembly.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya rājopagataṃ sabhātale; satrapraticchannam aripramāthinam virājamānaṃ parameṇa varcasā; sutaṃ mahendrasya gajendravikramam
english: The king, beholding him as he came upon the floor of the assembly hall — concealed beneath the appearance of a satra performer, yet a crusher of enemies, blazing with supreme radiance — saw the son of great Indra with the gait of a lord among elephants.

sanskrit: sarvān apṛcchac ca samīpacāriṇaḥ; kuto 'yam āyāti na me purā śrutaḥ na cainam ūcur viditaṃ tadā narāḥ; savismitaṃ vākyam idaṃ nṛpo 'bravīt
english: He questioned all those who moved near him: "From where does this one come? I have not heard of him before." The men did not tell him — they did not know. Then the king, full of wonder, spoke these words.

sanskrit: sarvopapannaḥ puruṣo manoramaḥ; śyāmo yuvā vāraṇayūthapopamaḥ vimucya kambū parihāṭake śubhe; vimucya veṇīm apinahya kuṇḍale
english: "This man is endowed with every quality, charming to the mind, dark and young, like a lordly elephant in his herd. He has put off his conch-shell bangles and bracelets, undone his braid and fastened on earrings —"

sanskrit: śikhī sukeśaḥ paridhāya cānyathā; bhavasva dhanvī kavacī śarī tathā āruhya yānaṃ paridhāvatāṃ bhavān; sutaiḥ samo me bhava vā mayā samaḥ
english: "— wearing a crest and fine hair in another fashion. Become an archer, put on armor, take up arrows too; mount a chariot and ride about. Be equal to my sons or equal to me!"

sanskrit: vṛddho hy ahaṃ vai parihārakāmaḥ; sarvān matsyāṃs tarasā pālayasva naivaṃvidhāḥ klībarūpā bhavanti; kathaṃ caneti pratibhāti me manaḥ
english: "For I am old and desire relief from burdens — swiftly protect all the Matsyas! Those of eunuch form are never of this kind, it seems to my mind."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca gāyāmi nṛtyāmy atha vādayāmi; bhadro 'smi nṛtte kuśalo 'smi gīte tvam uttarāyāḥ paridatsva māṃ svayaṃ; bhavāmi devyā naradeva nartakaḥ
english: Arjuna said: "I sing, I dance, and I play instruments; I am skilled in dancing, I am expert in singing. Assign me yourself to Uttara — I will be the dancing-teacher of the princess, O king of men."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu rūpaṃ mama yena kiṃ nu tat; prakīrtayitvā bhṛśaśokavardhanam bṛhannaḍāṃ vai naradeva viddhi māṃ; sutaṃ sutāṃ vā pitṛmātṛvarjitām
english: "But this form of mine — what would proclaiming it accomplish? It would only greatly increase grief. Know me, O king of men, as Brihannada — as a son or daughter bereft of both father and mother."

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca dadāmi te hanta varaṃ bṛhannaḍe; sutāṃ ca me nartaya yāś ca tādṛśīḥ idaṃ tu te karma samaṃ na me mataṃ; samudranemiṃ pṛthivīṃ tvam arhasi
english: Virata said: "Very well, Brihannada, I grant you the boon — teach my daughter and those like her to dance. Yet I do not think this work befits you; you deserve the earth girdled by the sea."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca bṛhannaḍāṃ tām abhivīkṣya matsyarāṭ; kalāsu nṛtte ca tathaiva vādite apuṃstvam apy asya niśamya ca sthiraṃ; tataḥ kumārīpuram utsasarja tam
english: Vaishampayana said: The king of the Matsyas, having observed Brihannada's skills in the arts, in dancing, and likewise in instrumental music, and having ascertained the certainty of his eunuchhood, then dismissed him to the women's quarter of the princesses.

sanskrit: sa śikṣayām āsa ca gītavāditaṃ; sutāṃ virāṭasya dhanaṃjayaḥ prabhuḥ sakhīś ca tasyāḥ paricārikās tathā; priyaś ca tāsāṃ sa babhūva pāṇḍavaḥ
english: And the lordly Dhananjaya instructed the daughter of Virata in singing and playing instruments, as well as her companions and attendants; and that Pandava became dear to them all.

sanskrit: tathā sa satreṇa dhanaṃjayo 'vasat; priyāṇi kurvan saha tābhir ātmavān tathāgataṃ tatra na jajñire janā; bahiścarā vāpy athavāntarecarāḥ
english: Thus Dhananjaya, self-controlled, dwelt there under his disguise, doing what was pleasing to those women; and the people there — whether those who moved outside or those within — did not come to know him for what he was.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca athāparo 'dṛśyata pāṇḍavaḥ prabhur; virāṭarājñas turagān samīkṣataḥ tam āpatantaṃ dadṛśe pṛthagjano; vimuktam abhrād iva sūryamaṇḍalam
english: Vaishampayana said: Then another Pandava, a lord, appeared as King Virata was inspecting his horses. The common people saw him approach like the solar orb freed from cloud.

sanskrit: sa vai hayān aikṣata tāṃs tatas tataḥ; samīkṣamāṇaṃ ca dadarśa matsyarāṭ tato 'bravīt tān anugān amitrahā; kuto 'yam āyāti naro 'maraprabhaḥ
english: He indeed gazed at the horses here and there; and the king of the Matsyas saw him gazing. Then the slayer of enemies spoke to his attendants: "From where does this man come, shining like an immortal?"

sanskrit: ayaṃ hayān vīkṣati māmakān dṛḍhaṃ; dhruvaṃ hayajño bhavitā vicakṣaṇaḥ praveśyatām eṣa samīpam āśu me; vibhāti vīro hi yathāmaras tathā
english: "This one gazes at my horses most intently — he must certainly be a skilled knower of horses, an expert. Let him be brought swiftly near me; for this hero shines just as an immortal would."
